The relationship between the OIC and UN-AOC is based on a shared understanding that dialogue among civilizations, cultures and religions is not simply desirable, it is essential to building peaceful, cohesive and resilient societies. For many years, our two institutions have worked within this common vision. The OIC and UN Alliance of Civilizations have maintained a long-standing cooperation framework and have repeatedly expressed their readiness to strengthen it through practical initiatives. Excellencies, this cooperation has particular importance today in the context of the continuing rise of Islamophobia and anti-Muslim hatred. Islamophobia cannot be addressed only after discrimination, incitement, or violence has already occurred. It must also be addressed at the level of where perceptions, stereotypes and narratives are formed. This is precisely where the contribution of the UN Alliance of Civilizations is particularly important. Through its work on intercultural and interfaith dialogue, UN Alliance of Civilizations helps create Spaces in which communities can encounter one another, not through stereotypes, political polarization, or fear, but through direct dialogue, mutual understanding, and human connection. Too often, differences are presented as threats rather than as opportunities for understanding. And increasingly, digital platforms can amplify stereotypes and misinformation on a scale that traditional dialogue mechanisms cannot easily match. In this environment, initiatives that build trust between communities are more important than ever. The OIC strongly believes that dialogue is not a substitute for human rights, but it is an important complement for them. We need both effective protection against discrimination and violence and sustained engagement that addresses the prejudices and misconceptions that allow such discrimination to develop. Excellencies, the OIC therefore highly values UN Alliance of Civilizations work in bringing together governments, religious leaders, civil society, young people and other stakeholders. Excellencies, I am particularly encouraged that our cooperation is receiving renewed attention at the highest level. Excellencies, ladies and gentlemen, dear colleagues, first of all, I would like to thank the co-chairs, Spain and Turkey, for convening this high-level meeting. Article 18 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights reminds us that everyone has the right to freedom of thought, conscience and religion. Protecting individuals, therefore, also means protecting their ability to practice their faith together with others, to maintain religious communities and institutions, and to express their beliefs peacefully in public as well as in private. This is particularly important at a time when antisemitism, anti-Christian hatred, anti-Muslim hatred, and other forms of religious intolerance continue to affect communities around the world. Our response must not be to push religion out of the public sphere. Rather, we should create societies in which different convictions can coexist peacefully and contribute to the common good. The Alliance of Civilizations has a unique role in this endeavor, building bridges where others see division and keeping dialogue alive where political circumstances make it increasingly difficult. Hungary remains committed to this mission because ultimately, dialogue among civilizations is not an abstract diplomatic exercise. It's one of the foundations upon which peace can be built.
